flags: The estimate neglects turning and other mowing overhead.
This is a mowing-time estimate that neglects turning time and small first-pass or boundary effects.

question: Moe uses a mower to cut his rectangular \(90\)-foot by \(150\)-foot lawn. The swath he cuts is \(28\) inches wide, but he overlaps each cut by \(4\) inches to make sure that no grass is missed. He walks at the rate of \(5000\) feet per hour while pushing the mower. Which of the following is closest to the number of hours it will take Moe to mow his lawn?
solution:
For the requested estimate, assume straight parallel passes and neglect turning time and small first-pass and boundary adjustments. The overlapping part cuts grass already mowed, so the effective width of new grass cut is
\[
28-4=24\text{ inches}=2\text{ feet}.
\]
The lawn has area \(90\cdot150=13{,}500\) square feet. Since a strip's area is its width times its length, dividing this area by the effective width gives an estimated walking distance of
\[
\frac{13{,}500}{2}=6750\text{ feet}.
\]
Time equals distance divided by speed, so the mowing time is approximately
\[
\frac{6750}{5000}=1.35\text{ hours}.
\]
Thus the closest choice is \(1.35\) hours, choice C.
